key_insight: A small independent checker converts admissible potential and exactly charge-conserving current fields into guaranteed error bounds, regardless of which PDE solver produced them.
engineering_relevance: Certificate-based verification can audit third-party, LLM-written, and neural PDE solvers without relying on code inspection or grid convergence alone.
method: Require solver outputs to include an admissible potential and an exactly charge-conserving current.
Independently check the certificate against a written physics specification to obtain guaranteed error bounds.
Apply the same checker to finite-element solvers, deliberately buggy implementations, LLM-generated solvers, and neural surrogates.
evidence_signal: The checker rejected or refuted all five bugs despite passing grid-convergence studies; reduced-basis neural predictions achieved bounds at most 0.0021% wide in-range and 0.3–25% wide out-of-range, where 90% conformal intervals covered none of 14 tests.
watch_item: Guarantees apply only to the stated physics model; informative bounds require energy-accurate outputs on a sufficiently resolving grid, and free-nodal neural predictions yielded valid but uninformative bounds.
paper_title: Verifying the Outputs of PDE Solvers: From Finite Elements to Neural Surrogates
